private_theorem_20_lines:
1. Let P be the original ordered nonempty byte patterns, with their original prefix arrays.
2. Before byte b, original state q_i is the length of the retained matched prefix of pattern i.
3. The induction invariant is identical q_i, hit counts, encoded-byte counts and write counts.
4. The active index inventory contains exactly those i with q_i>0, once, in original order.
5. Bucket B_b contains exactly original indices whose pattern[0]==b, once, in original order.
6. Snapshot C={i:q_i>0} union {i:q_i==0 and i in B_b} BEFORE any transition.
7. These sets are disjoint, so candidate count never exceeds P.
8. Merge the ordered lists to retain the original full-scan index order.
9. Consider omitted i: q_i==0 and pattern_i[0]!=b.
10. Original fallback while(q_i>0) has zero iterations for this i.
11. Original first-byte equality is false, so matched remains zero.
12. Since pattern length is positive, matched cannot equal pattern length.
13. The omitted transition therefore emits no hit and leaves q_i unchanged at zero.
14. Its original activeStates adjustment is also a no-op.
15. Every included i executes the EXACT original fallback/equality/hit/overlap/counter/state body.
16. Per-pattern transitions depend only on this byte, its own state, pattern and prefix array.
17. Original relative index order preserves hit-counter overflow/failure observation ordering.
18. Rebuild the active index list only from each candidate resulting matched>0.
19. Omitted states remain zero; the rebuilt inventory is exact and equals original activeStates.
20. Thus induction preserves all states/hits and split/overlap behavior for every byte sequence.
